skill.name: flow-nexus-neural
skill.description: Guide Flow Nexus neural training, inference, templates, and distributed clusters through MCP workflows.
skill.summary: Use Flow Nexus MCP workflows to train, deploy, monitor, and publish neural models.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline backtick formatting, and Flow Nexus MCP examples. One prerequisite block and one final note instruct users to run unpinned npx flow-nexus@latest commands, which creates a real external-command and supply-chain risk. The hardcoded URLs are documentation or authentication references, and the system reconnaissance hits are neural training fields.

remediation.issue: Unpinned Flow Nexus MCP setup command
remediation.suggestion: Pin a specific Flow Nexus package version or use a verified installation path. Explain how users can verify the package source before running it.

remediation.issue: External service authentication and tool permissions
remediation.suggestion: Document required permissions, token storage expectations, and data handling for Flow Nexus before users train or publish models.
Add confirmation guidance for resource costs and template publication settings before distributed training or model publishing.

content.user_title: Train Distributed Neural Models with Flow Nexus
content.value_statement: Neural training across sandboxes is hard to coordinate. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows for Flow Nexus training, inference, templates, and clusters.
actual_capabilities: Shows Flow Nexus MCP setup and authentication commands for the user.
Provides neural training examples for feedforward, LSTM, transformer, GAN, and autoencoder models.
Demonstrates model inference, benchmarking, validation, publishing, rating, and template marketplace workflows.
Provides distributed training cluster examples with node deployment, topology connection, status monitoring, and termination.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for stalled training, low accuracy, and memory pressure.
limitations: Requires a Flow Nexus account and a configured Flow Nexus MCP server.
Examples must be adapted to real datasets, model IDs, user IDs, and compute quotas.
The skill does not validate datasets, credentials, costs, or model ownership.
Distributed training depends on Flow Nexus and E2B service availability.

use_cases.title: Prototype Neural Models
use_cases.description: Create small training configurations before investing in larger model runs.

use_cases.title: Reuse Marketplace Templates
use_cases.description: Find, deploy, test, and rate Flow Nexus templates for common model tasks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Distributed Training
use_cases.description: Plan clusters, worker nodes, monitoring, and termination for large model jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Training Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to prepare a small feedforward training plan. Include tier, layers, training settings, and fields I must replace.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy and Test a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to select a marketplace template for my task, deploy it, run inference, and summarize validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Distributed Cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to design a distributed training cluster with topology, worker roles, monitoring, and a safe termination plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Federated Training Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to plan a federated learning workflow. Include node assumptions, aggregation rounds, privacy checks, and validation milestones.

output_examples.input: I need a small classifier prototype.
output_examples.output: A compact feedforward setup with tier guidance, layer choices, training parameters, and replacement fields for user ID and dataset.

output_examples.input: I want to evaluate a sentiment template.
output_examples.output: A template selection plan with deployment steps, inference checks, expected metrics, and rating guidance after validation.

output_examples.input: I need distributed training for image data.
output_examples.output: A cluster plan with node roles, topology choice, training settings, monitoring checks, and cleanup steps.

best_practices: Start with nano or mini tiers before moving to distributed clusters.
Pin and verify the Flow Nexus package before adding the MCP server.
Monitor job status, benchmark results, and validation output before publishing a model.
anti_patterns: Do not run unpinned setup commands in sensitive environments without reviewing package provenance.
Do not train with private or regulated data until authentication, retention, and isolation are confirmed.
Do not publish templates without validation, benchmark, and ownership checks.

faq.question: Does this skill train models by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides Flow Nexus MCP workflows that require a configured server and user authorization.

faq.question: Which model architectures are covered?
faq.answer: It covers feedforward, LSTM, transformer, GAN, autoencoder, and distributed cluster examples.

faq.question: Can I use marketplace templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows how to list, deploy, validate, rate, and publish Flow Nexus templates.

faq.question: Does it support distributed training?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes cluster initialization, node deployment, topology connection, monitoring, inference, and termination examples.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: A Flow Nexus account and authenticated MCP server are required before training, deployment, or publishing workflows can run.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review package provenance, compute costs, data sensitivity, service permissions, and model publishing settings.
